Impromptu Talk Principle 2: Give An Impromptu Talk Principle 2: It is simply a brief talk on a subject the speaker knowssomething about but for which they have had little time to prepare (p. 43).
Impromptu Talk Principle 3: Give An Impromptu Talk Principle 3: Chances are, you may find yourself in this situation a couple of times a week in school (p. 43).

Impromptu Talk Principle 4: Give An Impromptu Talk Principle 4: Suppose you are at a Scout meeting and the Scoutmasterasks you, without warning, to tell the troop about plans foran upcoming campout to Three Rivers State (p. 43).
step_by_step_procedure: Step 1 (Impromptu Talk): Step 1 (Give An Impromptu Talk): Think for a moment what you know about the campout, then quicklyorganize your thoughts (p. 43).
Step 2 (Impromptu Talk): Step 2 (Give An Impromptu Talk): Don't be afraid to pause for a second and reflect on thequestion or topic you have been asked to present (p. 43).
Step 3 (Impromptu Talk): Step 3 (Give An Impromptu Talk): Remind Scouts at the end of your speech to check with their folks about volunteering as chaperones (p. 43).
Step 4 (Impromptu Talk): Step 4 (Give An Impromptu Talk): You probablywon't be asked to talk about a topic you don't know somethingabout (p. 43).

You know parliamentary procedure by leading Principle 2: While the leader of an informal meeting may participatein the discussion, the chair of a formal meeting only conducts the meeting (p. 45).
You know parliamentary procedure by leading Principle 3: Speakers must be recognized by the chair andtechnically, all remarks are directed to the chair (p. 45).
You know parliamentary procedure by leading Principle 4: Questions from individual to individual also are directed via the chair (p. 45).
step_by_step_procedure: Step 1 (You know parliamentary procedure by leading): The formal meeting is more a debate of opposing ideas, each of which strives for audience approval (p. 45).

Step 2 (You know parliamentary procedure by leading): The chair enforces the rules equally on all participants to ensure thateach person has a fair opportunity to present his or her point of view (p. 45).
Step 3 (You know parliamentary procedure by leading): Responsibility for keeping themeeting goingalso meanskeeping itfocused (p. 45).

Step 4 (You know parliamentary procedure by leading): When the discussion While informal discussions do not have rules, the chair mustapply commonsense ideas for a successful meeting to takeplace (p. 45).
